assessments.reasoning: agpl_terms [28300,28765) states the trigger, audience, exact-version object, prominence, network location, price, and copying method. Its wording requires an opportunity to obtain source. A user's decision to decline it does not defeat an otherwise adequate offer.

agpl_terms [3327,3594) treats copying from or adapting the work in a manner requiring copyright permission as modification, with an express exception for exact copying. Installing an exact copy alone therefore fails the modification test.

agpl_terms [5264,6955) ties Corresponding Source to what is needed to generate, install, run an executable, and modify the particular work, subject to its exclusions. An upstream archive missing the deployed modifications or necessary build scripts fails that test. For source-form distribution the relevant source is the same work.

challenge.method: Varied the modification, remote capability, audience, visibility, price, and version of the offered source independently. Compared the operative sentence with the preamble's broader description of public server use.
challenge.results: Running an unchanged copy does not itself trigger this modification-based duty. A modified version lacking remote interaction has no such remote offer to make. Every actual remote user is in scope even on a private network. A noninteracting person falls outside the specified audience. A prominent free network download by customary means can satisfy the access condition. A fee for source or an obscure offer fails its respective condition. Even a prominent free archive fails if it supplies only another version's source.

limitations: Determining who modified a version, who interacts with it, how visible the offer is, and whether the source matches requires evidence about the deployment.
reasoning: When the licensee modifies the Program and that version supports remote network interaction, AGPLv3 §13 requires the version to prominently offer every user interacting with it remotely access to its Corresponding Source. The source must be available from a network server without charge through a standard or customary means of copying software.
